paragraphs: There was once a little girl who was stubborn and curious. When her parents told her to do anything, she disobeyed them, so how could things go well for her? One day she told them, ‘I’ve heard so much about Madam Trude that I’m going to visit her one day. People say everything about her looks so strange, and there are such odd things in her house, that I’ve become very curious!’ Her parents strictly forbade it. ‘Madam Trude is a bad woman who does wicked things,’ they said. ‘If you go to her, you’re no longer our child.’ But their ban did not stop the girl, and she went to Madam Trude anyway. When she arrived, Madam Trude said, ‘Why are you so pale?’ ‘Oh,’ she replied, trembling all over, ‘I’ve been so frightened by what I’ve seen.’ ‘What have you seen?’ ‘I saw a black man on your steps.’ ‘That was a charcoal burner.’ ‘Then I saw a green man.’ ‘That was a hunter.’ ‘After that I saw a blood-red man.’ ‘That was a butcher.’ ‘Oh, Madam Trude, I was terrified. I looked through the window and saw not you but, as I truly believe, the devil himself with a head of fire.’ ‘Oho!’ she said. ‘Then you’ve seen the witch in her proper clothes. I’ve been waiting for you and wanting you for a long time already. You shall give me some light.’ Then she turned the girl into a block of wood and threw it into the fire. When it was blazing fully, she sat down close to it, warmed herself, and said, ‘That’s a bright blaze for once.’
